title: Color histogram descriptors — Image Similarity Search
description: A color histogram counts pixels per quantized color bin, giving a compact global signature of an image. Histograms ignore layout, so two different beach photos match while a beach and a forest do not. They are cheap to compute and surprisingly effective for coarse similarity.
demo:
# Image similarity: cosine similarity over feature vectors (color/texture descriptors).
import math
images = {'img1': [8,2,1,1], 'img2': [7,3,1,1], 'img3': [1,1,8,2], 'img4': [2,1,1,8]}
def cosine(a, b):
    dot = sum(x*y for x, y in zip(a, b))
    na = math.sqrt(sum(x*x for x in a)); nb = math.sqrt(sum(x*x for x in b))
    return dot / (na * nb) if na and nb else 0.0
query = "img1"
qv = images[query]
ranked = sorted(((cosine(qv, v), name) for name, v in images.items() if name != query), reverse=True)
print("Query image:", query)
for score, name in ranked[:3]:
    print(f"  {name}: similarity {score:.3f}")
provenance: Public methodology — standard computer-science technique documented in the technical literature; fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Perceptual hashing — Image Similarity Search
description: Perceptual hashes shrink an image to a short bit string (e.g. 64 bits) where similar images differ in few bits. Hamming distance between hashes gives near-duplicate detection in constant time per comparison. Hashes are tiny enough to index billions of images.
